All confirmed as full enumerations that would go stale. I have enough to answer confidently.

**Source files** (would fail to compile / be incomplete without updates):
- `src/types/api.ts` — defines the `ErrorCode` union itself; a new member is added here.
- `src/lib/errors.ts` — `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE: Readonly<Record<ErrorCode, number>>` is an exhaustive record keyed by `ErrorCode`; TypeScript requires a new entry for the added code.

**Docs that enumerate the closed union in full** (would become inaccurate/stale):
- `docs/glossary.md` — spells out all nine codes with their HTTP statuses under "Error code".
- `docs/design/data-flow.md` — DES-025 lists the full `ErrorCode` enumeration.
- `docs/design/action-wrapper-and-errors.md` — DES-222 states "one of the nine `ErrorCode` values."
- `docs/adr/ADR-014-domain-errors-to-error-codes.md` — explicitly documents `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` as "covering exactly nine codes" and lists them all as the closed union.
- `docs/api/actions-overview.md` — has a full thrown-class → `ErrorCode` → HTTP status table plus a summary line declaring "the nine `ErrorCode` values."

Other docs (per-service/per-action error lists like `docs/api/actions-*.md`, `docs/design/service-*.md`) only cite the specific codes relevant to that action/service and don't enumerate the closed set, so they don't need updating unless the new error applies to them specifically.

ANSWER: src/types/api.ts, src/lib/errors.ts, docs/glossary.md, docs/design/data-flow.md, docs/design/action-wrapper-and-errors.md, docs/adr/ADR-014-domain-errors-to-error-codes.md, docs/api/actions-overview.md
